correctness.rationale: For p<=2 a least-norm coordinate plus a Hilbert-orthogonal unit vector gives the lower bound, and the scalar function 1-a^p+(1+a^2)^(p/2) is decreasing. At the balanced base point, concavity of t^(p/2) and convexity of c -> (a^2+c^(2/p))^(p/2) make the symmetric sum maximal at a simplex vertex, yielding the matching upper bound. For p>=2, coordinatewise orthogonal copies give both distances exactly sqrt(2); a one-coordinate base vector and the monotonic scalar bound give the reverse inequality. The p=2 and n=1 boundaries agree.
